title: Reconcile accepted documents into project terminology
summary: Retain per-project Annals document intake, obtain a restricted Nucleus proposal, and commit validated effects or an explicit no-change result with durable recovery.
use_when: Accepted-document coverage, relevance, semantic commits, no-change outcomes, or intake recovery must be understood.
Historical assignment or failed intake should be inspected or retried through supported controls.
do_not_use_when: Only repository terminology or project lifecycle should be read.
A Clockwork scheduling halt or installation rollback should be operated without first inspecting the product result.
outcome: A durable per-project intake outcome backed by exact source identity, validated append-only effects or no-change evidence, and an exact tool receipt.
effects: The scanner retains complete document bytes and per-project source identities atomically with scan cursor advance.
A worker processes at most one reconciliation, submits a restricted Nucleus job, and may commit effects or record no change.
Assignment is audited; retry creates a new attempt only after positively terminal prior-job evidence.
authority: Semantics owns per-project intake, routing policy, cursor durability, effect validation, receipts, domain success, and retries.
Annals owns accepted bytes and feed identities/order. Nucleus owns execution and mailbox transport; the agent interprets relevance under frozen instructions.
success: Validated effects and the exact receipt commit atomically before acknowledgement.
An empty effect list records examined HEAD, ends as ignored, and creates no semantic revision.
failure_and_recovery: Changed identities or fixed-page replay, nonadvancement, and cycles fail closed.
Ambiguous transport reuses the same retained requester/job and exact request. Conflicting tool redelivery fails.
Retry refuses an active or unprovable admitted prior job. Preserve committed revisions after runtime failure.

A scheduled dependency or reconciliation failure ends the current invocation. The shared service-health threshold delays a new scheduling halt; later activations preserve exact request correlation, prior commits and explicit retry authority.
privacy: Complete source documents and selected repository snapshots are private retained state and are supplied to Nucleus without workspace, shell, or web access.
Logs exclude source/project bodies, raw dependency diagnostics, paths, prompts, credentials, diffs, commands, and tool values.
does_not_authorize: Direct SQLite mutation, manufactured cursors, cleared correlations, a direct-Codex fallback, upstream mutations, or disclosure.

consumers.statement: Local operators and public typed clients inspect intake or apply authorized routing/retry controls; the selected private worker performs reconciliation.

preconditions.statement: Work requires exact configured Annals library and project cursors, valid participation, compatible Nucleus execution, complete selected Bazaar instructions, normal admission, and serial worker ownership.

inputs.statement: Input is complete accepted document text with immutable library/event/document identity, filename, digest, acceptance time, project, opaque cursor, selected repository HEAD, and frozen request/instructions.

outputs.statement: The semantics CLI prints plain text by default. --json selects the existing compact command-specific JSON schema and coded failures on stderr. The typed client and pinned worker explicitly request JSON; machine callers must pass --json. Output schemas, retained state, effects and exit statuses are unchanged.

Intake status exposes separate annals_decision_accounts and legacy_decisions collections, fixed routing outcome, assignment, state, attempts, request correlation, and domain outcome. New empty-effect completion records no_change_revision and no applied_revision.

data_semantics.statement: New local intake IDs are per project; embedded Annals IDs remain original. Agents decide relevance without an origin/cwd filter. Historical sources, grounds, assignments, states, requests, and decoders retain their meanings.

identity_and_units.statement: Library/event/document identifies the exact upstream source; project-local intake identifies one reconciliation; requester/job and call digest bind immutable transport/recovery. Cursors are opaque.
No independent model pricing or consumption unit is defined.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Coverage starts after each project activation watermark. Every retained document and cursor advance commit together. Fixed pages contain at most 200 events and 4 MiB of document bytes; only empty is end-of-prefix.
No source-acceptance-to-semantic-revision wall-clock bound is promised.

access.statement: Supported operations use local-user state and published read-only upstream interfaces. Nucleus receives neutral cwd, workspace none, no shell/web, and one immutable managed tool.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Worker execution is cross-process serial; paused projects reject late commits. Effect validation precedes atomic revision/receipt commit and mailbox acknowledgement. Identical redelivery is idempotent and conflicts fail.
One requester/job survives ambiguous transport; explicit retry requires positively terminal prior-job evidence and preserves frozen instruction selection.

operational_limits.statement: Each worker invocation processes at most one reconciliation. New document jobs use semantics/semantic-document-reconciliation/1 and permit no-change results.
No throughput, storage capacity, retention, or source-to-commit latency objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Schema 3 preserves historical sources, states, correlation/receipt bytes, cursors, revisions and old tool/ground identities. New document contracts have distinct immutable identities and migration reinterprets no history.
No general future support or deprecation window is promised.

reliances.statement: Reconciliation reads complete documents and opaque cursors from one exact Annals decisions library.
Nucleus executes a restricted proposal and durable tool exchange; Semantics retains domain validation and commit authority.

Bazaar owns shared selection format, exact component loading, rendering, and trusted description expansion. Semantics chooses its component set and owns authored meaning, runtime inputs, typed request and toolset assembly, permissions, execution, domain effects, and recovery. Prepared text grants no additional authority.
Project lifecycle and repository replay determine valid intake and semantic effects.
